title: Queue harmonic reservoir for tail smoothing and admission resilience
creator: Maya Patel
description: Background: we observe recurring p99 spikes during short bursts and mixed-length workloads. Investigation shows pathological interactions between admission windows (prefill gating), kernel choice heuristics, and attention optimization paths which cause small batches to be scheduled on slower kernels, amplifying tail latency. This ticket pilots a queue-level reservoir that smooths admission by dynamically borrowing capacity from low-priority prefills and applying controlled graceful drops to maintain latency SLOs while preserving throughput and cost targets.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Queue Harmonic Reservoir (QHR): a lightweight admission layer that maintains a slowly-adapting reservoir value per-GPU-pool. QHR will: 1) compute a harmonic mean-based budget across recent batch shapes and kernel latencies; 2) bias admission to co-locate requests that improve kernel match probability; 3) provide a probabilistic graceful-drop policy when budget is depleted; 4) emit metrics for per-step kernel-choice skew and reservoir pressure. This integrates with kernel selection by providing kernel-aware admission hints (preferred target kernel family) rather than hard routing.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: reduces p99 spikes without heavy over-provisioning; provides observability into admission pressure; preserves aggregate throughput.
- Cons: adds complexity to admission path and a tuned hyperparameter (reservoir decay); graceful drops can impact perceived availability for low-priority traffic.
- Unknowns: interaction with KV-cache warmups (prefill vs decode) — may need an additional warmup bypass for cache-heavy requests.
milestones: M1: prototype QHR as admission middleware and instrument kernel-choice metrics (2026-02-28)
M2: run A/B on staging traffic with simulated burst profiles and measure p95/p99 (2026-03-10)
M3: refine drop-rate policy and add kernel-hint integration (2026-03-17)
M4: gradual rollout to dedicated pools with canary and rollback triggers (2026-03-24)
acceptance_criteria: A1: p99 token latency reduced by >=30% on mixed-length burst tests vs baseline in staging (measured over 24h)
A2: end-to-end throughput within -5% of baseline under sustained load
A3: no increase in 5xx error rate attributable to QHR after rollout
A4: dashboard with reservoir pressure, kernel-hint match rate, and graceful-drop_rate exposed to Console
testing_plan: Unit tests for reservoir math and decay semantics
Integrations: run closed-loop simulator with trace-replay of production traffic and kernel-latency models
Staging canary: 1% traffic for 24h, 10% for 72h, compare p95/p99 and throughput
Fault injection: force kernel mismatch and simulate KV-cache cold starts to validate bypass and stability
rollout_plan: Canary rollout with automated rollback if p99 worsens by >10% or 5xx increases by >0.5%. Start with non-customer facing pools, then Dedicated test tenants, finally Hosted API low-tier. Observability gating via runtime-1.23 dashboard and alerting rules.
